claim_verdicts.evidence: "The standard ListView constructor works well for small lists ... In contrast to the default ListView constructor, which requires creating all items at once, the ListView.builder() constructor creates items as they're scrolled onto the screen." The children argument is an ordinary Dart list expression, evaluated before the constructor call, i.e. on every run of the enclosing build (Dart semantics).

Docs: "you can build the items on demand as they scroll into view" (scrolling); "use the lazy builder methods, with callbacks. That ensures that only the visible portion of the screen is built at startup time" (perf). Run at stage-3 code (Flutter 3.47.2), 10 000 products, box 360x400, 48 px rows: built ids [1..14] (9 on stage), i.e. visible rows plus a few beyond the edge; 'Product 100' 0 widgets incl. offstage.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/flutter-website .../ui/layout/scrolling/index.md; .../perf/best-practices.md ('Be lazy!'); flutter test probe in DonHang.App

claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution (probe test against stage-3 ProductCatalog, skipOffstage: false): at start ProductTile ids [1..14]; after tester.drag(-20000) ids [412..431] only (rows 1-14 removed); after dragging back to top ids [1..14] again, i.e. built again on return. ProductTile is a StatelessWidget with no keep-alive request. The docs mirror has no sentence on element disposal; evidence is the run.
claim_verdicts.source: flutter test probe in examples/don-hang/DonHang.App (Flutter 3.47.2), files lib/widgets/product_catalog.dart, product_tile.dart @ stage-3

claim_verdicts.evidence: "When you have a long list of items in your ListView or GridView (including an infinite list), you can build the items on demand as they scroll into view ... check out ListView.builder or GridView.builder." Execution: same 10 000 products at width 900 (GridView.builder branch, 3 columns) built 20 ProductTile in total.

git show stage-3:DonHang.App/test/product_catalog_test.dart lines 56-69: 10000 products, `SizedBox(width: 360, height: 400, ...)`, `expect(find.text('Product 1'), findsOneWidget)`, `expect(find.text('Product 10000'), findsNothing)`, `expect(tester.widgetList(find.byType(ProductTile)).length, lessThan(30))`. find.byType skips offstage by default, so the count is on-screen tiles (9 of 14 built); round-2 text now says 'on screen'.

`flutter test test/product_catalog_test.dart` in DonHang.App (working files identical to stage-3 for catalog, tile and test): last line `00:01 +4: All tests passed!`. Probe with the same widget tree: find.text('Product 100') evaluates to 0 widgets, also with skipOffstage: false, so `findsOneWidget` on it fails.

Extended claim (round 3, s5 new sentence). Docs mirror: "children of a viewport that are currently not visible in the viewport are now considered off-stage. To find them in a test, specify `skipOffstage: false` on the Finder." Run at stage-3, width 360, 48 px rows: height 400 -> 9 on stage, 14 built incl. offstage (5 more beyond the edge); heights 200/560 -> 5/10 and 12/17. So the finder skips the few rows built past the edge, and built tiles stay far below 10 000.

Conditional recommendation, not a bare ranking. Docs: "When you have a long list of items ... you can build the items on demand as they scroll into view. This provides a much more performant scrolling experience." Run: 10 000 products, 14 tiles built. issues.text: Carried from round 2, narrowed. The new sentence tells me built tiles are the on-screen ones plus 'only a few more', which I can follow. But it also tells me the finder skips off-screen rows. Then if every product had a tile, the thousands off screen would be skipped too, so the third check (and 'Product 10000' finding nothing) would still pass. I can no longer see how this test 'checks this'; the 'few tiles built' part seems to come from section 4, not from the test.
issues.quote: The finder skips the rows built just beyond the edge, because they are off screen, but those are only a few more, so the tiles that exist also stay far below 10 000.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after 'stay far below 10 000.' saying whether this test would still pass if every product had a tile, and, if it would, that the few-tiles-built conclusion comes from how the builder works (section 4), while the checks only show which tiles are on screen.
